comments: Blackness was glorious this morning.  There seemed to be two distinct flocks.  By my clicker count, at daybreak I had 1852 Pink-footed at the mouth of the Midhope Burn below Abercorn, where I had set up before first light. As it got lighter, it was apparent that there was also a large number of geese on the west side of the bay near the castle.  As it got lighter, I counted 1353 by the castle, but I'm less confident of that count as it was at distance. About 0750, a fisherman flushed another 492 from around the west of the castle, and they flew in from that direction and joined the castle flock. Small groups from both flocks started to disperse about 0805. They appeared to be headed opposite directions, with some minor intermingling.  At 0817 most of the geese from the burn mouth flew east and that pattern continued. Geese from the castle side seemed to head to adjacent fields mostly.  Most geese had dispersed mostly by 0850, but there were about 500 still grazing on shrinking mudflats with rising tide when I left at 0930.  I only had Pink-foots, no other geese species observed, though I was pleased to see there were about 320 Wigeon and lots of waders and gulls.
